items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the cleared board); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The phase 6 objective gains a reach-quality term, so a road tier is something it can see
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-08: "Roads should be visible in phase 6 too." The ruling is written into GENERATION_STRATEGY.md as the objective's FIFTH TERM; this item is the work.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED IT (archived NR-793, confirmed on a live ten-market world, seed ABCDEF01, every term alive):
  tier=1  IN_REACH=25658  raws=122  composite=0.010256174
  tier=3  IN_REACH=26024  raws=122  composite=0.010256174
The reach frontier moves by 366 tiles. Every scored term is bit-identical.

THE CAUSE IS ONE NUMBER, and it is raws_in_reach: 122 either side. A road tier scales traversal COST, continuously. Terms 1 and 4 read reach through a PER-RESOURCE COVERAGE BOOLEAN - is there any reachable deposit of resource R in this catchment - and that boolean is SATURATED. With 122 resource-market pairs already covered across 25,658 tiles, 366 more tiles introduce no pair that was not already covered. So the axis moves a continuous quantity the objective only reads through a threshold, and the search spends a third of every round proposing a change it cannot score.

THE CONSTRAINT, and it is the whole difficulty. Cheaper traversal everywhere is trivially better, so a reach-quality term entered as a FLAT VIABILITY BONUS would reward a uniformly well-connected map - precisely the evenness term 3 and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable exist to prevent. The term must be a PER-MARKET reading whose SPREAD is scored, exactly like terms 1 and 2, never a single global number added to the composite.

SLICE 1 IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A FEATURE, and it decides what the term reads. Two candidates: the mean traversal cost from a market to the tiles in its catchment, and the in-reach tile COUNT rather than the coverage boolean. Both are continuous and both move when a tier does. Score candidates that differ ONLY in road tier and ask whether the chosen reading DISCRIMINATES between them at all. A reading that does not is not worth keeping, and that is an afternoon's answer rather than a wasted build. This is § The first slice is the scorer applied to the new term.

TWO THINGS TO CARRY, both from the archived phase 6 work. (1) The default-seed phase 6 fixture is a TWO-MARKET world on which balance and composite evaluate to zero for every candidate - it is not a sound basis for any phase 6 measurement, and NR-793's first reading was taken on it before being re-run on a live world. Use a 10-15 market world. (2) Adding a term changes every ranking and therefore the selected landscape, so this is a world-moving change and owes the digest discipline in DELIVERY.md § The digest re-bless is one act per WAVE.

DONE WHEN: road tier 1, 2 and 3 produce DIFFERENT composites on a 10-15 market world; the difference is reported per market rather than as one global number; an even-reach landscape does not beat an uneven one at the same mean; and the determinism of the argmax is unchanged across thread counts.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Leans per pass - named forces over the ancient and industrial spans, resolved against the seed
items.design:
BEN'S CALL (2026-09-08): yes, leans per pass - the wizard's preferences model extended past planetology.

THE MODEL IS UNCHANGED AND MUST STAY UNCHANGED: a lean is a NAMED LEAN on an axis, resolved against the seed by a resolve_* function, and no raw generated value is editable. It names a FORCE, never an outcome - the tune-the-forces-never-the-outcome rule is not relaxed for being player-facing, and 'guarantee me an empire' is exactly the reading it forbids.

WHAT THE AXES ARE IS THE DESIGN WORK OF THIS ITEM, and it is NOT settled. Each candidate axis must map onto a scalar the sim ALREADY reads, or it is a new mechanism wearing a lean's clothes. The obvious candidates to test: consolidation pressure (fractious vs consolidating) and sea legs (insular vs seafaring) for pass 1; industrialisation timing (late vs early) and tariff posture (open vs protective) for pass 2. A lean whose effect is not visible on the round's own globe is not worth offering.

DONE WHEN: each shipped axis moves a measurable outcome across a SEED SWEEP - not one seed - and none of them clamps.
items.notes: SUPERSEDED IN ITS AXES by BL-839 (2026-09-08): Ben named the axis he actually wants - HISTORICAL TURBULENCE, fewer or more countries at the epoch. The four axes guessed at here (consolidation, sea legs, industrialisation timing, tariff posture) were explicitly unsettled and are now second to that one. Keep this item for the round 5 / pass 2 leans; round 4 lean is BL-839.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Round 5 - metros, reach across water, firm markers and charters, and the market carve
items.design:
FOUR OBJECTS, ALL FOUR CHOSEN BY BEN (2026-09-08), drawn in order on the epoch globe: metros growing out of the population centres the history grew and sacked; colonial reach across water; firm markers with their charters; the market carve and its price field.

THIS ROUND SHOWS THE SELECTED LANDSCAPE, NOT THE SEARCH. Phase 6 scores candidates statically in milliseconds; a ranking is not a spectacle. The player watches the winner being drawn.

PLACEHOLDERS ARE EXPECTED AND ARE THE POINT. Phase 6's search is not built (BL-770 was cancelled with the board clear) and colonial ties do not cross the handoff yet. Each of the four draws from whatever is real today - centres, corporations and markets all are; reach across water is the one with nothing behind it - and is LABELLED as a placeholder where it is one. An unlabelled placeholder is a lie the next session will believe.

THIS PAYS THREE OF THE FOUR OWED VISIBILITY ITEMS: the region surface, the market-carving explanation, and background firms - the last of which stops being blocked by the worker-thread objection, because a wizard round is not the worker's loading screen.

DONE WHEN: all four draw in the built app on a LIVE click-through, each placeholder is visibly marked as one, and the Visibility table's verdicts are updated to match what actually renders.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the visibility form: extra wizard rounds, leans per pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The wait becomes the round - run the real pass inside rounds 4 and 5, drawing as it computes
items.design:
THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM THIS ITEM EXISTS FOR. The planetology rounds re-run their chain as a pure throwaway preview on EVERY control move. The history sim is the most expensive pass in the project and cannot be previewed that way at any budget - so rounds 4 and 5 invert the wizard's own mechanism, and that inversion needs stating rather than discovering.

THE SHAPE: the player sets the leans, presses Run, and the pass runs INSIDE the round with its output drawn as it computes. Accept moves on; reroll runs it again. The generation_progress sink already exists for the loading screen and is the natural feed; what changes is that generation stops being one call behind a bar and becomes calls the player initiates.

BEN'S RULING THAT LICENSES IT (2026-09-08): 'a watched wait needs no budget' - which is why the whole startup-budget chain was dropped rather than deferred.

AND THE OBLIGATION THAT REPLACES THE BUDGET IS SHARPER, NOT LOOSER. A watched wait must be WORTH WATCHING. A round that shows a still globe for ninety seconds is worse than the bar it replaced, because the bar at least admitted it was a wait. If the playback has dead stretches, the answer is to make them move - never to hide them behind a caption.

START_NEW_GAME IS THE SEAM THAT MOVES. The one-and-only generation call splits, and the clock rebase at handoff must still hold: wall time spent watching must not land as elapsed in-game days.

DONE WHEN: a live click-through from the menu to play, timed, with no stretch longer than a few seconds in which nothing on the globe changes.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, describing round 4 against the live app); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Research points accrue from population - the parked placeholder, stated as one
items.design:
BEN PARKED THE DESIGN AND NAMED THE STUB (2026-09-08): "We want to simulate research as well, however we will have to park that. Instead of designing it, allow research points to accumulate based on that culture's population."

SO THIS ITEM IS DELIBERATELY TINY AND MUST STAY TINY. Points accrue in proportion to population. No tree, no rates, no unlocks, no per-culture modifier - every one of those is the design that was parked, and adding any of them here is how a placeholder quietly becomes the system nobody chose.

IT MUST BE LABELLED AS A PLACEHOLDER wherever it surfaces - in the code and on BL-821's leaderboard. An unlabelled placeholder is a lie the next session will believe.

DONE WHEN: research points exist, accrue from population, and every surface showing them says what they are.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, describing round 4 against the live app); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The levers that keep round 4 multipolar - culture, logistics, communication, succession
items.design:
RETURNED TO THE POOL 2026-09-09, unbuilt and unchanged. This was planned for sprint 36 and never started. Ben redirected that sprint mid-flight: the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and this item is EMPIRE-PHASE - it only bites once there is something to fight over. Applying it to a span that is overwhelmingly settlement (839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0, measured) is what would force the fixture-fitting the redirect exists to avoid. Re-scope it against whatever phase boundary sprint 37 settles on before building it.

BEN ASKED FOR LEVERS THAT STOP A TOTAL HEGEMON and named two - cultures in region, and a simple logistics implementation - leaving the rest to judgement. They serve BL-224's non-hegemony invariant, and the constraint on every one of them is the standing rule: a lever is a FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE ON THE MAP, never a term inside an actor and never a penalty that scales with a polity's rank.

THE SIX, with what exists today. (1) CULTURES IN A REGION - foreign-culture ground costs cohesion to hold and assimilates slowly, so conquest buys unrest rather than strength. PARTLY BUILT: w_cult = 150 and a per-region culture index are already in history_sim.hpp, so this is calibration more than construction. (2) SIMPLE LOGISTICS - reach falls with distance from the seat along real terrain, so a campaign past reach cannot be sustained. This is the lever that makes a strait or a mountain stall a frontier WITHOUT special-casing either, which is why it is worth more than its cost. OWED. (3) COMMUNICATION - a polity cannot act on ground it cannot hear from until a communication rung is reached. OWED, and it is also the second rung of Ben's own arc, so it earns its place twice. (4) SUCCESSION - a large polity fractures on a leadership transition, weighted by cohesion; this is the dark-age rung. COLLAPSE.md already owns culmination. (5) STRAIN - already built, and its accumulators already cross the pass 1 -> pass 2 handoff. (6) BALANCING COALITIONS - neighbours' stance moves against the largest polity.

LEVER 6 IS THE DANGEROUS ONE and is called out rather than dropped. It is one step from an agent handicap: a coefficient that reads a polity's rank and pushes back is exactly the shape the standing rule forbids. It is admissible ONLY as a STANCE the player can read on the map (RELATIONS.md), arrived at by an in-world cause. If it cannot be built that way, it is not built.

DONE WHEN: across a SEED SWEEP - not one seed - a single polity holding the great majority of the world's land at 1200 CE is rare rather than typical, and each shipped lever demonstrably moves that distribution when varied. A world that does produce a near-hegemon stays a legitimate outcome; the levers tune the forces, they do not clamp the result.

BEN'S ENDING SPEC, 2026-09-09 (elicitation notes): 'this phase will feed directly into our industrial era sim, where we see resources as capital, so it's important to keep in mind specifically how larger empires may persist, expand their reach, and then collapse into smaller nations ready for an industrial boom.'

THAT MAKES NON-HEGEMONY AN INPUT REQUIREMENT, not just a watchability one. Pass 2 is an economy pass over NATIONS, and nations are what an empire leaves behind when it can no longer hold itself. So a world ending pass 1 as one hegemon has failed the handoff however plausible its numbers -- and so has a world that never assembled anything larger than a city state. Both ends produce an industrial era with nothing to industrialise against.

REACH-GATING IS NOW THE PRIMARY LEVER, and it changes this item's shape. BL-837 was settled on 2026-09-09 as a GATE rather than a price, so lever (2) is no longer 'simple logistics' among six -- an empire persists while its network holds and fragments when it does not, and the number of nations at 1200 CE is a consequence of what got built and stayed maintainable. Re-read the other five as SUPPORTING that mechanism rather than substituting for it, and drop any that only duplicate it.

NEVER A TARGET COUNT AND NEVER A COLLAPSE EVENT FIRED AT A DATE.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08: get the sim right first - grudges, cultural mixes, provinces owned); Claude (itemisation, against the sim as it stands)
items.title: State what pass 1 hands on, as one structure, and assert nothing else crosses
items.design:
"THE IMPORTANT PART IS THAT WE TAKE BACK SOMETHING USEFUL" (Ben, 2026-09-08). This item is that sentence made checkable.

GENERATION_STRATEGY.md already names what crosses each handoff and adds 'and nothing else'. That clause is currently a promise in prose with nothing enforcing it. Pass 1 now produces three more things - grudges, cultural mixes, and the provinces each polity holds - and a fourth pass will want a fifth thing unless the boundary is written down as a TYPE.

THE WORK: one struct that is the whole of what pass 1 hands forward, with every consumer taking it rather than reaching into the sim state. Then the doc's list and the struct's fields are the same list, and a change to either shows up as a change to the other.

WHY IT IS WORTH A SEPARATE ITEM rather than a tidy-up inside BL-826: a handoff that is a struct is the difference between 'the history informed the world' and 'the history IS the world's cause'. It is also what makes pass 1 re-runnable in a wizard round without dragging the entire sim state into the UI layer.

DONE WHEN: one type carries the handoff, no consumer reaches past it, and the doc's list matches its fields.
items.resolution: PARTIALLY DELIVERED and closed as partial rather than complete, on the author's own admission. pass_one_output, make_pass_one_output and pass_one_output_valid exist and are asserted by tools/verify/pass_one_handoff.cpp (C7a-C7h, 0 failures, re-run in the main session). What is NOT done is the item's actual point: settlement_seed_polities, generate_nations and hard_coded_world still reach into settlement_state and history_sim_state directly rather than taking the struct, so "every consumer takes it, and nothing else crosses" is still a promise in prose. The review barrier confirmed the remainder is INCOMPLETE rather than INCONSISTENT - no consumer reads a field whose meaning changed under it - so it is safe to leave, and it is the seam BL-843 also wants (the load path skips pass_one_output_valid, which already checks what the seam does not). Re-file the rewiring with the stage 4 work.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08: another focused pass on economy from 1560 to 1960); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Pass 2 as the economy pass - 1560 to 1960, on the calendar Ben stated
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-08: "another focused pass on economy from 1560 to 1960". With pass 1 ending at 1200 CE that fixes the whole calendar - and the calendar is now STATED rather than derived from a boundary-year default.

THE CONSEQUENCE THAT IS NOT A DETAIL: epoch_year = 1960 puts the campaign in the INDUSTRIAL era band. era_band_for_epoch flips at 1700, so every consumer keyed on the band - eras, the resource split, the unit roster - takes the industrial branch rather than the ancient one that epoch_year = 0 produced. That is a world-moving change and it owes the digest discipline in DELIVERY.md: one deliberate re-bless against a stated description of what changed.

THE 1200 -> 1560 GAP IS A COAST, NOT A HOLE. Pass 1's arc ends in a stable dark age, and a span defined by little changing is the one span not worth simulating. The world arrives at 1560 holding what 1200 left it. What this item must check is whether anything ACCUMULATING is silently lost across it - assimilation shares (BL-826) and grudge decay (BL-827) are the two that move on their own - and advance those cheaply across the gap rather than stepping it.

SAME ENGINE, DIFFERENT QUESTION. Pass 1 asks who holds what ground. Pass 2 asks what that ground produces and trades. The works roster is cumulative and the unit roster is era-keyed, so this is the first span continued with more rows offered - not a second mechanism (§ Three passes of simulated history).

DONE WHEN: a full run does 3,600 years to 1200 (2400 BCE -> 1200 CE, divided at 400 BCE -- BL-871, Ben 2026-09-09; the earlier figure here was 4000), coasts to 1560, runs 1560-1960, and arrives at an industrial-band epoch; the accumulators crossing the gap are named and handled; and the era-band flip is deliberately re-blessed rather than absorbed.

PASS 1'S TOTAL CHANGED UNDER THIS ITEM, 2026-09-09: 3,600 years rather than 4,000, starting 2400 BCE. THE 1200 -> 1560 COAST AND THE 1960 EPOCH ARE UNAFFECTED -- only pass 1's start and its internal boundary moved. The accumulator question this item raises for the 1200 -> 1560 gap now applies a second time, at the 400 BCE boundary inside pass 1 (BL-871).

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08: another focused pass on economy from 1560 to 1960); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Colonial ties - reach across water in pass 2, and the trade relationships it leaves behind
items.design:
WHAT PASS 2 ADDS OVER PASS 1 is reach across water - a campaign or settle target across a sea leg, staged from harbour works, because colonisation by a major is the Metropole strategy played overseas. It culminates as every major does (../lore/COLLAPSE.md), and the epoch still arrives multipolar: the non-hegemony invariant is NOT relaxed for the sea.

WHAT IT LEAVES BEHIND is the part that matters to the campaign, and it is already named in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md as crossing the handoff: COLONIAL TIES seed the order book's preferred-seller relationships, so a colony's chains close through its metropole before they close anywhere else.

THAT IS ONE OF THE THREE IN-WORLD FORCES the design relies on to make market conditions uneven WITHOUT a term inside an agent - tariffs, distance, and ties. A player can read why on the map, which is the whole test.

AND IT IS ALSO ROUND 5'S SECOND OBJECT: reach across water is the one of BL-819's four with nothing behind it today. This item is what turns that placeholder into a real drawing.

DONE WHEN: colonisation happens across water on a seeded sweep without producing a hegemon; ties survive the handoff into the order book; and round 5 draws real reach rather than a labelled stub.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08: another focused pass on economy from 1560 to 1960); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Tariff posture out of pass 2, enacted as an ordinary import_tariff law
items.design:
A NATION THAT INDUSTRIALISED LATE RELATIVE TO ITS NEIGHBOURS PROTECTS WHAT IT HAS. That is the cause; the posture is its consequence, and pass 2 already computes the input - polity::industrial_year, the year a polity crossed the rung, is in history_sim.hpp today.

WHAT MATTERS IS HOW IT IS ENACTED: as an ORDINARY import_tariff law at world setup, not as a special generation-only field. The design says so explicitly, and the reason is the one that keeps the whole economy legible - a player can open the law panel and read the tariff, repeal it, and watch prices move. A hidden generation modifier would be invisible and unrepealable, which is the shape the standing rule against invisible forces exists to prevent.

RELATIVE, NOT ABSOLUTE. 'Late' means late against its neighbours, so a world where everyone industrialised late produces no protectionists - which is correct, and is why the term must not be a threshold on the raw year.

DONE WHEN: postures derive from relative industrialisation dates, land as real import_tariff laws visible in the law panel, and a world with uniform timing produces no tariffs.

items.author: Found by the BL-826 regression hunt (2026-09-08); Claude
items.title: Winter can never win a tie in the season argmax, and integer truncation makes ties common
items.design:
THE SEASON AXIS IS DECIDED BY A STRICT COMPARISON. Summer is evaluated first (w = 0) and winter guards on s > best_score - strictly greater - so an EXACT TIE always keeps summer.

WINTER'S ONLY BENEFIT IN THE SCORE is that def_ready drops 1000 -> 750, shrinking the defence term (params.w_def * def_eff) / 2000. That is integer division, so on a weak defender the winter advantage TRUNCATES TO ZERO and the two seasons tie exactly - at which point the strict comparison silently discards winter. Measured: def_scaled must reach about 4 before the winter delta survives the divide at all.

Against a zero-defence target both terms are 0, so winter is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a hair. That is why R5 reports 0 winter campaigns out of 258 with the winter premium set to 0 to make winter freely competitive. The scoring itself is healthy where a defender exists - probed candidates show winter strictly ahead (s=70 vs 67, s=83 vs 81) - the argmax simply never reaches them while a dead region outranks everything.

SO THIS IS THE SECOND-ORDER HALF AND IT IS SEQUENCED DELIBERATELY. Fixing BL-835 may make R5 pass on its own by removing the dominating candidate. Fix BL-835 first, RE-MEASURE, and only then decide whether the tie-break also wants changing - a tie-break altered while a bigger distortion is still in play is a change nobody can evaluate.

AND THE TIE-BREAK IS A DESIGN CALL, not a defect to silently flip. Preferring summer on a tie may be exactly right. What is wrong is that it is UNSTATED and that truncation manufactures the ties.

DONE WHEN: BL-835 is fixed and R5 re-measured; the tie-break is then either stated as deliberate in MILITARY_HISTORY.md or changed on Ben's ruling.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the holistic scorer: diplomacy, logistics, turbulence); Claude
items.title: Simple logistics and ancient roads - so that holding ground has a cost that falls off with distance
items.design:
RETURNED TO THE POOL 2026-09-09, unbuilt and unchanged. This was planned for sprint 36 and never started. Ben redirected that sprint mid-flight: the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and this item is EMPIRE-PHASE - it only bites once there is something to fight over. Applying it to a span that is overwhelmingly settlement (839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0, measured) is what would force the fixture-fitting the redirect exists to avoid. Re-scope it against whatever phase boundary sprint 37 settles on before building it.

BEN, 2026-09-08: "this is also why we need basic logistics and ancient roads". It is the answer to the scorer's question A - CAN I KEEP THIS REGION - and under BL-835's civilian/army split that sharpens to CAN I KEEP AN ARMY THERE.

WITHOUT A REACH COST THAT FALLS OFF WITH DISTANCE OVER REAL TERRAIN, HOLDING IS FREE, and the only limit on an empire is how fast it can walk. That is the whole of why the non-hegemony invariant currently has to be defended by other means.

A ROAD IS THEN THE THING THAT MAKES A FRONTIER STAY WHERE IT IS. Ancient roads extend sustainable reach along their line, so an empire's shape becomes a consequence of its infrastructure rather than of a radius - which is the mechanism that makes a strait, a mountain range or an unroaded interior stall a frontier WITHOUT any of them being special-cased.

SOME OF THIS EXISTS. rebuild_reach already computes terrain-weighted distance from a capital by Dijkstra, using logistics.cpp landform ratios. What it does not do is BIND that reach to whether force can be sustained - it is an input to scoring, not a constraint on holding. Read BL-834 first: that cache is rebuilt 12,000 times in a 4000-year run and reach is already 66-86% of the run, so anything that makes reach load-bearing must be built on the fixed cache, not the current one.

DONE WHEN: an army beyond sustainable reach cannot be maintained; a road tier visibly changes where a frontier settles; and an unroaded interior stalls expansion without a radius rule.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-09, elicitation): REACH GATES A CAMPAIGN; IT DOES NOT MERELY PRICE IT. Beyond sustainable reach a campaign is not an expensive option, it is not an option. The pricing alternative -- let a polity overextend and then collapse -- was recommended and was DECLINED, and that is recorded because it explains what the ruling buys.

GATING MAKES THE ROAD THE MECHANISM INSTEAD OF THE FLAVOUR. If reach only priced a campaign, a rich polity could buy its way past geography and a road would be a discount. Gated, the only way to reach further is to BUILD further -- so an empire's shape is the shape of what it built, and this item stops being a modifier and becomes the empire phase's spine.

IT IS THE SHAPE THE SIM ALREADY USES. MILITARY_HISTORY.md sec Forage gates rather than prices: a force forages where it is adjacent to water or to land its own polity owns, and starves where it is not. Reach-gating is that rule generalised off the coast and onto the road, not a new kind of constraint.

BEN'S OUTCOME BRIEF (2026-09-09, elicitation notes) NAMES THIS ITEM'S REAL DELIVERABLE: 'a sparse road network which connects city-states, forms empires, and gives us actual population centres, derived by possible supply and governance'. The phase's output is a NETWORK -- nodes are seats (BL-866), edges are roads -- and its extent is the reason an empire is the size it is. See BL-872 for the centres half.

RE-SCOPED AGAINST THE PHASE BOUNDARY the returned-to-pool note asked for: the boundary is 400 BCE -> 1200 CE (BL-871, revised by Ben the same day from 0 CE), and this item belongs wholly inside it.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the holistic scorer: diplomacy, logistics, turbulence); Claude
items.title: Neighbours coalesce against a riser out of fear of being next - the scorer second question
items.design:
RETURNED TO THE POOL 2026-09-09, unbuilt and unchanged. This was planned for sprint 36 and never started. Ben redirected that sprint mid-flight: the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and this item is EMPIRE-PHASE - it only bites once there is something to fight over. Applying it to a span that is overwhelmingly settlement (839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0, measured) is what would force the fixture-fitting the redirect exists to avoid. Re-scope it against whatever phase boundary sprint 37 settles on before building it.

BEN, 2026-09-08, giving the balancing-coalition lever the cause it was missing: the scorer must ask "will others attack me for fear of being wiped out next?"

THIS IS WHAT MAKES THE LEVER ADMISSIBLE, and the distinction is the whole point rather than a technicality. GENERATION_STRATEGY.md marked balancing coalitions the DANGEROUS lever, because a term that reads a polity's RANK and pushes back is an agent handicap in a diplomacy costume - precisely the shape the standing rule against agent handicaps forbids. Fear of annihilation reads a BEHAVIOUR instead: what this polity has actually done, to whom, on ground a player can point at.

THE RECORD IT READS ALREADY EXISTS. BL-827's grudge ledger is directed, decaying, and carries named events with a place and a date. A coalition forming against a riser is therefore explicable on the map - the player can ask WHY and get a list of what that polity did - which is the bar every in-world force in this project has to clear.

IT MUST NOT BECOME A RANK TERM BY THE BACK DOOR. 'Largest polity' is not the trigger; 'the polity that has been doing this to people like me' is. A quiet reimplementation as a size coefficient would pass every test here and violate the rule the item exists to satisfy - so the check must be that a large but peaceful polity attracts NO coalition, while a smaller aggressive one does.

AND IT IS BASIC, DELIBERATELY. This is a fear response inside the Era -1 sim, not a diplomacy layer: no treaties, no negotiation, no alliance objects. Two of BL-827's four grudge kinds ('a union refused', 'an ally abandoned') remain unbuilt for exactly that reason and stay unbuilt here.

DONE WHEN: a large peaceful polity attracts no coalition and a smaller aggressive one does; the coalition's cause is printable as the events behind it; and hegemony frequency falls across a seed sweep without any term reading size.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-08, on the holistic scorer: diplomacy, logistics, turbulence); Claude
items.title: Historical turbulence as the round 4 lean - roll for a world with fewer or more countries
items.design:
RETURNED TO THE POOL 2026-09-09, unbuilt and unchanged. This was planned for sprint 36 and never started. Ben redirected that sprint mid-flight: the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and this item is EMPIRE-PHASE - it only bites once there is something to fight over. Applying it to a span that is overwhelmingly settlement (839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0, measured) is what would force the fixture-fitting the redirect exists to avoid. Re-scope it against whatever phase boundary sprint 37 settles on before building it.

BEN, 2026-09-08: "we are really looking to encourage historical turbulence as a parameter - so that players can roll for worlds which have fewer countries at this step, or more countries at this step".

THIS SUPERSEDES BL-818's PLACEHOLDER AXES. That item said the axes were the design work and were not settled; this is the settlement, and it is a better axis than any of the four guessed at, because the player can WATCH it resolve on the very map round 4 is showing them. A lean whose effect is invisible on its own round is not worth offering.

IT TUNES FORCES AND NEVER CLAMPS A COUNT. A turbulence lean moves the SPREAD of culture aggression, how sharply neighbours coalesce against a riser (BL-838), and how fast reach decays with distance (BL-837). It does not target a number of nations, and it must not acquire a post-hoc correction that does. The 2026-07-30 emergent-nation-count ruling, BL-224's non-hegemony invariant and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable all survive intact: fragmented or consolidated is an OUTCOME, not a quota.

CULTURE AGGRESSION IS WHERE THE TUNING LANDS. polity::aggression_q already exists, derived from the culture's own aggression_q (BL-277 Q5). Two archetypes are worth having and they are not the same shape: one that EXPANDS AND INCORPORATES, absorbing the conquered and growing large and durable; one that CYCLES - unifying, stabilising, fragmenting and re-unifying on a rhythm. The same engine produces different turbulence signatures from them, which is why a SPREAD of aggression profiles is worth more than a single dial.

THE STANDING RULE APPLIES AND IS NOT SOFTENED. Both archetypes are drawn from real history as MECHANISMS, exactly as HISTORY.md's institutional ladder is. What transfers is the mechanism; a proper noun never does. No generated name in Io is Earth-derived, and this item must not become a name bank - see GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Real history in, invented names out.

DONE WHEN: the lean moves the epoch nation-count DISTRIBUTION across a seed sweep in the expected direction, at both settings, with no term targeting a count; and a world at either setting is still a legitimate world.

items.author: The sprint 35 step 4a review barrier (2026-09-08); Claude
items.title: The realm-ended grudge can never fire - its predicate is unsatisfiable
items.design:
FOUND BY THE STEP 4a REVIEW BARRIER, and it is the exact defect a barrier exists to catch: a harness green on a feature that does not exist.

extinguish_polity (history_sim.cpp:602) raises grudge_kind::realm_ended only from surviving polities that SHARE THE DEAD REALM'S CULTURE. But polities are seeded ONE PER DISTINCT CULTURE (lines 396-427, deduped with std::find) and polities.push_back occurs at line 427 and nowhere else in the file. So for any surviving kin, kin.culture != dead_culture is ALWAYS true and the loop body is never reached.

CONSEQUENCES. params.grudge_realm_ended = 900 - the LARGEST magnitude in the whole table - is never applied. grudge_event_line's "a realm ended" string is unreachable. And the documented behaviour in history_sim.hpp - "the dead leave a grudge in their kin, never in an heir" - is unimplemented prose. The seed-0 fixture extinguishes several realms and produces zero realm_ended events.

tools/verify/pass_one_handoff.cpp ASSERTS NOTHING ABOUT realm_ended, which is why it passed 0 failures over a dead branch. Whatever the fix, it owes an assertion that this kind actually fires.

THE FIX IS A DESIGN CALL, not a repair, because the original ruling was reasoned FROM the one-polity-per-culture fact: the dead leave a grudge in their kin rather than an heir, precisely because there are no heirs. If kin cannot exist either, the choice is between dropping the kind outright and giving it a different bearer - the dead realm's NEIGHBOURS, say, who watched it happen, which is also the natural feed for BL-838 (fear of being next).

DONE WHEN: either the kind is removed with its magnitude and its string, or it fires on a real run and a harness asserts that it does.

items.author: The sprint 35 step 4a review barrier (2026-09-08); Claude
items.title: A holder with no free culture slot loses its assimilation into the anonymous tail
items.design:
FOUND BY THE STEP 4a REVIEW BARRIER. It silently disables the anti-hegemony lever BL-826 exists to build, on exactly the ground where that lever matters most.

THE PATH. All three named slots hold A, B, C; a fourth culture D takes the region. shift_toward(D, ...) finds no slot for D (settlement.cpp:96), the displacement test taken > cw[smallest] fails while the smallest slot is bigger than one round's take, and line 112 puts the gain into other_q. share_of(D) reads the TAIL as 0, so the w_cult term (history_sim.cpp:1190) charges D the FULL foreign discount forever. The ground never digests.

AND THE ACCUMULATED GAIN IS PERMANENTLY LOST. When D finally does claim a slot it restarts from one round's take; the reviewer measured roughly 240 per-mille of assimilation stranded in a tail that is foreign to every culture and never re-attributed. The tail is documented as "peoples too small to name"; this path makes it a one-way sink for the HOLDER'S OWN share.

THIS IS THE COMMON CASE, NOT A CORNER. A frontier region changing hands three times is ordinary - and on the current fixture one region changes hands 258 times (BL-835).

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed: the holder's share is the one share that must be nameable, since it is the one every downstream reader asks about. Either the holder always claims a slot on first gain, or the tail tracks the holder separately from the anonymous remainder. Whichever, the invariant to state and then assert is that a share the sim is actively accruing is never written somewhere share_of cannot read it back.

DONE WHEN: a holder with three foreign slots digests its ground at the same rate as one with a free slot, and a harness asserts no accrued share is unreadable.

items.author: The sprint 35 step 4a review barrier (2026-09-08); Claude
items.title: Integer truncation freezes small grudges forever, falsifying both decay and sparsity
items.design:
FOUND BY THE STEP 4a REVIEW BARRIER. Two of the grudge design's stated properties are false in the code, and both were argued for in prose rather than measured.

THE ARITHMETIC. g.score -= (g.score * shed) / 1000 (history_sim.cpp:770) truncates to a ZERO decrement once score < 1000/shed. shed = grudge_decay_per_year_q (3) x step_years, so in the -20..0 band (step 5) shed is 15 and any score below 67 decrements by exactly nothing, forever. At the 4000-year span the -400..-100 band (step 20, shed 60) freezes everything below 17; the -100..-20 band (step 10, shed 30) freezes everything below 34.

SO A SINGLE border_raided (magnitude 60) raised late in a run is frozen at 60 for the rest of it. It never reaches grudge_floor (4), so it is never erased, and it crosses the handoff as a permanent row.

BOTH DESIGN CLAIMS FALL. The comment's "a half-life near 230 years, so a single old wrong is gone by the epoch" is true only for LARGE scores. And the sparse table the design is built on is not sparse: every pair that ever skirmished keeps a permanent row. Sparsity was one of the three reasons the ledger was affordable at 4000 years.

The usual fix is a minimum decrement of one where score is above the floor, but that changes the half-life at the bottom of the range and should be measured rather than assumed.

DONE WHEN: no score above grudge_floor is stationary across a round at any step_years in use, and a 4000-year run's grudge count is measured rather than asserted.

items.author: The sprint 35 step 4a review barrier (2026-09-08); Claude
items.title: The save seam checks the shares sum but not their structure, and a stricter checker already exists
items.design:
FOUND BY THE STEP 4a REVIEW BARRIER. r_region (save_game.cpp:351) enforces total_q() == 1000 and per-field ranges, but NOT the structural invariants every culture_shares accessor depends on: weight 0 exactly where id is -1, descending sort, no duplicate ids, ids in range.

THE FAILURE. A truncated or bit-flipped save carrying id = {-1, 5, -1}, weight_q = {1000, 0, 0}, other_q = 0 passes every current check and loads clean. The region then reports empty() == true and plurality() == -1 while carrying 1000 per-mille on an unnamed slot, and share_of(5) == 0 although slot 1 names culture 5. Every downstream reader - city_names.cpp:76, hard_coded_world.cpp:742, the polity seed at history_sim.cpp:399 - silently treats the region as uncultured.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS CHEAP AND SLIGHTLY EMBARRASSING: pass_one_output_valid() ALREADY CHECKS ALL FOUR (history_sim.cpp:2337-2379). The stricter checker exists and the load path does not call it. Two callers sharing one implementation is the discipline that stops a check measuring something different from the code - the same argument BL-775 was filed on.

NOTE THE SEVERITY HONESTLY: this is a corrupt-input hardening issue on a local single-player save, not a live exploit, and the save seam is not the untrusted wire boundary the standing rules govern. It is filed because the fix is small and the checker is already written.

DONE WHEN: the load path enforces the same four structural invariants as pass_one_output_valid, through one shared implementation rather than a second copy.

items.author: BL-835 verification (2026-09-09); Ben's call to file it separately; Claude
items.title: In the quiet worlds every battle is still a conquest, and nothing yet says why
items.design:
FILED ON BEN'S CALL when BL-835 was closed (2026-09-09): the pathology BL-835 was written against is gone, and what is left is a smaller and different question that deserves its own item rather than holding that one open.

WHAT WAS FIXED. BL-835 removed the cause of the dead-region ping-pong. The seed-0 fixture went from 258 battles on ONE zero-population region - battles == conquests == 258, exactly 1:1 - to 9 battles across a world that grows from 533 to 1,372 regions. The signature is gone.

WHAT REMAINS. Several seeds still show battles == conquests exactly. Measured on the merged tree: seed 0 at 9 battles / 8 conquests, and the world_determinism fixtures at 4/4 (seed A) and 65/49 (seed B), 30/13 (the 1960 arc). The worlds that DO fight at volume have broken the 1:1 ratio; the quiet worlds have not. At 4 to 9 battles across four thousand years the ratio may be nothing but small numbers - nine coin flips landing the same way is not evidence of a weighted coin - or it may be that in a world with almost no armies, any attack that is worth launching at all is one that cannot be resisted.

THE ITEM IS TO FIND OUT WHICH, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT BEFORE IT IS A FIX. Do not tune anything against the ratio until a seed sweep says whether it survives at volume. The instrument exists: history_sim_harness already prints battles and conquests unaided, and B384a ('every world sees at least one region change hands by war') and B384c currently FAIL because several seeds fight zero times - which is itself part of the same question.

RELATED AND POSSIBLY THE REAL ANSWER: Ben's 2026-09-09 observation that the rules for initial colonisation and the peaceful spreading of societies are vastly different from those of war and empire, and that stage 4 may want to be two phases rather than one. A span that is overwhelmingly settlement - 839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0 - being scored by empire-phase rules is a candidate explanation for every symptom in this item. See the sprint 37 goal.

DONE WHEN: a seed sweep says whether battles == conquests survives at volume, and either a cause is named or the ratio is recorded as small-number noise and the item closed.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, colonisation design form); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The settled cells become a binding input to the province partition
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09, ruling on the direct question: colonisation SEEDS the partition; the late pass still DRAWS it.

PROVINCES.md keeps its ordering (after the sim, before roads) and keeps its nation lock. What it gains is the colonisation span's settled cells and their anchors as a HARD INPUT, the way it already takes the national assignment.

THE ROAD NOT TAKEN, recorded so it is not rediscovered: colonisation drawing the REAL partition, with the nation carve then assigning whole provinces rather than tiles. That would make ruling 5's single-nation guarantee true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a check, and it answers Ben's own 2026-08-21 objection that packed provinces are 'scarcely how borders were defined in history'. It reorders the generation chain, which is why it was not taken now.

DONE WHEN: the partition reads the settled cells, P9c and the nation-lock scan still pass, and province shapes visibly follow settlement history rather than centre geometry alone.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, resolving NR-808); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The tribal marches retire and fragmentation is re-derived from how far two peoples mix
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09, resolving NR-808. COLONISATION.md's 'Fragmentation comes from contact' is the authority; this item is the work.

RETIRE: the tribal marches in creeds.cpp (the aggression-vs-defence comparison, the weld loop at creeds.cpp:236-287, and the fragmentation_q -= welds*120 with its half floor).

REPLACE WITH: fragmentation_q read off how far two peoples' streams interpenetrate. Two cultures whose shares mix heavily across a broad frontier are LESS fragmented; two that never met are MORE. The input is culture_shares, which the colonisation span already produces at every founding - so the same number comes out of a mechanism already running, with no roll and no pairwise war.

THE GRAIN WAS THE DEFECT, NOT THE TIMING. The marches compare cradle to cradle, a scalar against a scalar between two discrete points. Under diffusion a cradle is a SOURCE, not a point, and what meets at a frontier is two streams already mixing. Moving the marches past the boundary would have fixed when they ran and left that untouched.

WHAT SURVIVES: aggression_q, unchanged, as the Era -1 sim's DOCTRINE input. What it stops doing is setting the nation count. Consolidation now comes from package breadth - a people who spread far ends up one culture over a lot of ground. One cause each, where aggression previously drove both.

TWO THINGS THIS ITEM MUST NOT SKIP:
  1. THE NON-HEGEMONY FLOOR. The old welding was floored at half the incoming fragmentation      precisely so creeds alone could not manufacture a hegemon. The replacement needs its own      bound; a different mechanism does not make BL-224's invariant somebody else's problem.
  2. THE NATION COUNT MOVES, and it is a MEASUREMENT. fragmentation_q drives the seed budget      and the seed budget drives how many nations a world has. Measure the distribution across      a seed spread BEFORE the change lands - it cannot be reasoned to from the mechanism's      shape. world_audit R1/R3 and the creeds harness both read this path.

DOCS ALREADY UPDATED 2026-09-09: COLONISATION.md, CREEDS.md and HISTORY.md. The CODE comments (creeds.hpp:17/87/89, hard_coded_world.cpp:520) still describe welding and are correct until this lands - fix them WITH the change, not before.

DONE WHEN: no scalar-comparison war remains anywhere in the design, fragmentation derives from contact, the non-hegemony bound is re-derived and asserted, and the nation-count distribution is reported across a seed spread.

items.author: Sprint 37 build session (2026-09-09), raised while building BL-846; Claude
items.title: The sim's terrain view carries no rivers, so the colonisation walk cannot price the cheapest ground the design names
items.design:
THE GAP, FOUND BY BUILDING AGAINST IT. COLONISATION.md section The stream lists the cheap routes in order: river courses and coastal shelf are cheap - the routes people actually followed. The walk can price the shelf and CANNOT price a river.

WHY. A river in this codebase is an EDGE, not a tile: tile_component::river_edges is a six-bit side mask written by generate_rivers, and components.hpp is explicit that a river is an EDGE, never a tile. sim_terrain_view (history_sim.hpp) carries four parallel rasters - substrate, cover, density, landform - and no river among them. So the colonisation flood, which reads that view, has nothing to test.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT COSMETIC, and it is why this is its own item rather than a TODO. It is the difference between a history whose corridors are RIVERS and one whose corridors are SHORELINES. Under the shipped walk the cheapest route in the world is the coast, so every generated history is a maritime one and no interior river valley ever carries a stream faster than the open ground beside it. That contradicts the design's own first example.

WHAT TO BUILD: a fifth raster on sim_terrain_arrays - one byte per tile, non-zero where river_edges is non-zero - populated by build_sim_terrain from the same tile field, and a matching pointer on sim_terrain_view. colonisation_input::river already EXISTS and is already read by tile_year_cost (it prices a river tile at 35% of base against the shelf's 55%); it is null from every caller today. So this item wires an input that is built and tested, rather than adding a mechanism.

MIND THE COST OF THE VIEW. Adding a raster to sim_terrain_arrays costs one byte per tile (~31 KB on a homeworld) and nothing per year - it is fixed at generation and nothing rewrites it, exactly as substrate is.

DONE WHEN: colonisation_harness shows a river valley carrying a stream faster than the plain beside it; the share of reached land whose first arrival came along a river is reported; and world_determinism is unchanged (the raster is a new input to a pass that does not yet run in generation, so it must move nothing).

items.author: Sprint 37 build session (2026-09-09), on NEXT_SESSION.md's explicit instruction to raise rather than delete; Claude
items.title: history_sim_harness B384a asserts every world goes to war, which the colonisation design says is wrong
items.design:
B384a asserts that EVERY world sees at least one region change hands by war. It fails, and has failed for some time: measured this session at 5 of 8 worlds fighting, 5 of 8 taking ground, so three seeds fight zero times.

THE DESIGN NOW SAYS THAT IS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR. COLONISATION.md's whole premise is that the opening span is a SETTLEMENT process with occasional violence - the interesting question is not who wins but who arrives - and BL-846's own record measures the ancient span at 839 foundings against 9 battles on seed 0. A world that fills peacefully is a legitimate history, not a broken one. So the harness is asserting a claim the design has since overturned, and a check that fails for a correct reason is worse than no check: it trains the reader to ignore a failure line.

RAISED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DELETED, on NEXT_SESSION.md's explicit instruction. There is a real question underneath it that should not be lost with the assertion: the sim should still be CAPABLE of war, and B384b (the transfer branch fires somewhere in the set) is the assertion that actually checks that.

THE OPTIONS, and this needs Ben rather than a judgement call: (a) retire B384a outright, leaving B384b as the capability check; (b) restate it as a SET-LEVEL claim - some fraction of worlds fight - which is what the design implies and what B384b already half-says; (c) keep it and gate it on a params flag that only a war-heavy fixture sets. B384c (a polity somewhere loses its last region) is a separate failure with a separate cause and is NOT covered by this item.

DONE WHEN: history_sim_harness's baseline failure count reflects only real defects, and whichever assertion replaces B384a is one the colonisation design would endorse.

items.author: Sprint 37 region-count sensitivity measurement (2026-09-09), NR-809; Claude
items.title: The neighbour graph densifies as regions fill in, so region count still scales superlinearly after BL-844
items.design:
WHAT BL-844 LEFT STANDING, and it said so itself. BL-844 replaced the heapless reach scan with a heap and removed the O(N^2) per rebuild; its closing note records that ms/rebuild still rises with region count (0.017 at 529 regions -> 0.079 at 1,160 on seed 0) because the neighbour graph DENSIFIES as regions fill in, so edges are not O(N) in this world and O(E log V) still grows - and declines to pursue it further on the grounds that reach is no longer what a long run is made of.

RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY THIS SESSION and the figures reproduce exactly: seed 0 gives 0.017 / 0.045 / 0.079 ms per rebuild at 533 / 833 / 1,174 regions; seed 1 gives 0.035 / 0.114 / 0.218 at 563 / 931 / 1,260. Fitted exponent 1.95-2.27 across both seeds. Reach is 24-37% of a 4,000-year run (history_span_cost, build_gen /O2).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW, WHEN IT DID NOT BEFORE. Ben's sprint-37 brief asks to transform regions into provinces and not to aim for a small set - which spans a factor of SIXTEEN (1,372 regions against 22,153 land provinces). At an exponent of ~2 that is ~256x the reach term: seed 1's 6,541 ms run would spend roughly 400 SECONDS in reach alone. The region count is therefore capped by the ADJACENCY MODEL rather than by the pathfinder, and no further heap work reaches it.

THE SHAPE OF A FIX, none of it settled: region adjacency is Chebyshev at neighbour_radius 9 and water-blind, so a region gains neighbours as the map fills whether or not anything can move between them. Capping degree, or making adjacency a nearest-k rather than a radius, would make edges O(N) again. Both change what the sim considers a neighbour, which moves battles and campaigns - so this is a determinism-digest change and NOT a refactor.

NR-809 IS THE DECISION THIS ITEM HANGS OFF. If Ben caps the region count for this sprint (the recommendation), this stays filed and unbuilt. It is what a sixteen-fold count would need.

DONE WHEN: mean neighbour degree stops rising with region count, history_span_cost shows ms/rebuild flat across the span table, and world_determinism's digests are re-blessed deliberately rather than accidentally.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, watching round 4 at the live app); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Most of the land ends habitable and peopled, and emptiness stops being the default
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: we aim for most of the land to be habitable, and include human populations.

MEASURED: the first build leaves roughly HALF the homeworld permanently grey, and it is visible on screen as unclaimed ground that never fills. The harness reads 51-61% of land farmable across three seeds, and one seed (2) reached only 34% farmable with 62% of land reached at all.

EMPTINESS STAYS A REAL OUTCOME AND STOPS BEING THE DEFAULT ONE. COLONISATION.md's 'ground no package suits is not settled' is unchanged as a RULE. What changes is the calibration target it is measured against: a finished migration round should leave the map substantially peopled, with unsettled ground the exception marking genuinely hostile country.

THE FIX IS IN THE PACKAGE, NEVER IN A FLOOR THAT FILLS THE MAP REGARDLESS. The levers are what a package can farm (the affinity floor, currently 120 per-mille) and how it broadens -- both magnitudes, so this is history_sweep's to argue. A clamp that settles ground no package can farm would delete the frontier mechanism BL-847 exists to create, which is the failure mode this item must not produce.

DONE WHEN: history_sweep reports the habitable/peopled share across a seed spread, most land is peopled on most seeds, and the frontier still stalls somewhere on every world.

--- MEASURED 2026-09-09, AND IT OVERTURNS THIS ITEM'S PREMISE ---
The route work (BL-857) alone moved farmable share 50->56%, 46->52%, 34->43% across seeds 0/1/2. Rather than reach for the affinity floor to close the rest, a per-farm-class census of the UNFARMED remainder was added to colonisation_harness. It is decisive:

  seed 0  boreal 2154/3842 unfarmed, montane 241/275   (boreal = 45% of all unfarmed land)
  seed 1  boreal 2393/3400 unfarmed, montane 505/507   (boreal = 43%)
  seed 2  boreal  974/2055 unfarmed, montane 221/270   (boreal = 35%)

THE SHORTFALL IS POLAR ICE AND MOUNTAINS, NOT A BROKEN PACKAGE GATE. Boreal is cold ground (snow cover or icy substrate) and it is 24-30% of the whole homeworld -- the polar caps of a 261x121 grid. Montane is near-totally unfarmed and small. Both are exactly the classes that SHOULD be sparsely peopled, and no cradle forms in either, so no package carries affinity for them.

EXCLUDING BOREAL AND MONTANE, roughly 70% of reached temperate land is farmable on seed 0 -- which is 'most', as asked.

SO THE LEVER THIS ITEM NAMED IS THE WRONG ONE. Lowering package_affinity_floor would have raised the headline number by making cradle packages farm glaciers, satisfying the metric while deleting the frontier mechanism BL-847 exists to create. That is the exact failure the item's own text forbids, and the census is what caught it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN, and it is Ben's rather than a constant to tune: (a) accept it -- polar ice is not meant to be farmed, and 'most land habitable' should be read as most TEMPERATE land; (b) reduce how much of the map is boreal, which is a PLANETOLOGY question about ice-cap extent, not a colonisation one; or (c) let some packages coin cold affinity, which needs a cradle to form on cold ground and is a real design change.

The census is committed and reports rather than asserts, so the sweep can argue it.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, watching round 4 at the live app); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The 4000-year run fights zero battles, so the arc has no conquest in it
items.design:
FOUND BY DRIVING THE BUILT APP, 2026-09-09, and not by any harness.

THE READING: '0 battles, 0 conquests, 611 foundings in the full run' across four thousand years on seed 0, with five powers holding ground and none ever taking any from another. Ben's arc -- origin, communication, conquest or diplomatic union, a stable dark age -- has only its first act.

THE LIKELY CAUSE, and it needs confirming rather than assuming. Culture-by-route (BL-848) gives each stream a CONTIGUOUS block, so a region's neighbours are overwhelmingly kin; the objective scorer's w_cult discount for foreign ground therefore never fires. Large unclaimed buffers (BL-859) compound it by leaving polities without shared frontiers at all.

THE EVIDENCE IS AMBIGUOUS AND MUST NOT BE ARGUED FROM ONE ARC. At the 4000-year span battles fell 567 -> 70 after culture-by-route; on the 1960 two-span arc they ROSE 30 -> 141. Both are real measurements of different arcs. A tidy story about kinship suppressing war fits the first and not the second, so the cause is to be MEASURED across history_sweep before anything is changed.

THIS IS THE COUNTERWEIGHT TO BL-854. That item argues B384a (every world sees a region change hands by war) should be retired because a warless settlement span is correct behaviour. This item is the reason that argument cannot be taken on faith: a span with NO war in it at all is not a peaceful settlement process, it is a missing mechanism. Settle the two together.

DONE WHEN: the cause is measured rather than reasoned, and the history round (BL-860) produces conquest without the migration round being made violent.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the Empires design pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Population centres become settlements, and a settlement is a place worth taking
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: population centres become settlements, and settlements are SPARSE.

Today centres are drawn broadly across the map (POPULATION.md sec Generation). That is right for a populated world and wrong for a world of CITY STATES: if everywhere is a settlement, nowhere is a seat, and an empire is just a larger blob of the same stuff.

SPARSE MAKES CONQUEST MEAN SOMETHING. A settlement holds the stores, is where the muster forms, and taking it is how a war ends. Ground between settlements is HINTERLAND: it feeds a seat, is walked through, and changes hands when its seat does. A city state is a settlement plus its hinterland; an empire is a city state holding other settlements. No new actor type -- the sim's `polity` already is one.

OPEN AND NOT TO BE GUESSED: whether a settlement is a threshold on the existing urban record, a separate record, or a promotion of certain regions.

DONE WHEN: settlements are visibly sparse on the round-4 map, each has a hinterland that changes hands with it, and the count is stable across a seed spread.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-09, elicitation): A SETTLEMENT IS A SEAT FLAG ON A REGION, and every region points at the seat it feeds. No new table and no new id space -- the region already carries everything a seat needs to be worth taking (population, manpower_stock, army_stock, the four endowment windows, the urban record), so a separate settlement record would hold a pointer back to a region for every field that matters.

THE HINTERLAND IS A POINTER, and that is what makes it change hands with its seat. Ground is not conquered region by region; taking the seat takes what points at it. A region whose seat is gone is re-pointed at the conqueror's seat or falls outside anyone's reach -- which is how an empire's edge becomes ragged with no rule drawing a ragged edge.

region::centres IS NOT RETIRED BY THIS and is not the same question: centres are how many urban places stand on a region, the seat flag is which region a city state is governed from. A seat with no centre is a poor capital and a legitimate world.

DONE WHEN (revised): seats are visibly sparse on the round-4 map, every region resolves to a seat or to none, a taken seat carries its hinterland with it, and the seat count is stable across a seed spread.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the Empires design pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Materials are spent when something happens, and labour divides three ways
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: materials are spent when actions happen -- NOT via markets or buildings. And: a high population province must reserve population for work in industry to feed the settlements, raising a natural equilibrium between civilian and military strength.

NO ECONOMY, AND IT MUST NOT GROW ONE. No price, no order book, no firm, no building stack -- MARKETS.md and PRODUCTION.md own those and they belong to a later era. What this phase has is STORES AND EXPENDITURE: a polity holds materials, an action consumes them.

THE EQUILIBRIUM IS A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A DIAL. Labour divides three ways -- subsistence, industry, muster -- and the division is forced by what the ground and the population can bear. That is what makes conquest COST something without an economy: an army in the field is labour not farming and not making, so a polity that musters too hard starves or stops producing.

AN IN-WORLD FORCE WITH A VISIBLE CAUSE, which is this project's standing requirement for a brake -- never a term inside an agent's head.

OPEN: whether stores are per polity or per province. Ben's phrasing reads as per PROVINCE, which makes the labour split a property of ground rather than of a realm.

DONE WHEN: a campaign visibly costs materials and labour, a polity that over-musters is measurably worse off, and no market or building appears anywhere in the path.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-09, elicitation): THE STORES SIT AT THE SEAT, AND FALL WITH IT. Not one treasury per polity, and not a heap on every region. A seat holds what its hinterland produced; a conqueror who takes the seat takes the stores standing in it.

THAT CLOSES THE LOOP BETWEEN CONQUEST AND MATERIALS, and it is why BL-866 (settlements are sparse) has to land first -- there is nowhere to put a store until there is a seat. A war that ends by taking a city ends by taking that city's capacity to fight the next one, so a losing polity gets materially poorer rather than merely smaller: the shape polity::cohesion_q gives defeat, expressed in stock rather than in morale.

THE LABOUR SPLIT STAYS ON THE GROUND, because that is where the people are. Subsistence, industry and muster divide per region out of that region's own population; what industry makes flows to the seat. So the open 'per polity or per province' call is answered as BOTH, at different grains -- the split is a property of ground, the captured stock is a property of the seat.

DONE WHEN (revised): a campaign visibly costs materials and labour, taking a seat transfers its stores, a polity that over-musters is measurably worse off, and no market or building appears anywhere in the path.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the Empires design pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Some peoples grow armies and begin to conquer, and which ones is downstream of their route
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: depending on their creed, some cultures grow armies and begin to conquer.

THE INPUT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY EARNED. culture::aggression_q derives from the pantheon's war god, and COLONISATION.md sec Culture arrives by route made the distribution of pantheons a RECORD OF ROUTES. So which peoples turn warlike is downstream of where their ancestors walked -- which is exactly the ordering the colonisation design set out to establish: doctrine is downstream of how a people came to live where it lives.

NOT EVERY PEOPLE CONQUERS, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A world where every culture musters is as flat as one where none does.

NOT A NEW AI GRANT. A polity choosing to campaign is a decision, and this phase HAS actors where the migration span deliberately has none -- but it is the Era -1 sim's EXISTING scored-utility verb set, already covered by the dated register in AI_OPPONENT.md sec 11, bound by the same constraints: pure, seeded, deterministic, replayable, only legal verbs, never a planner. ANYTHING BEYOND THOSE FIVE VERBS IS A NEW WIDENING AND IS BEN'S TO GIVE -- raised, never assumed.

DONE WHEN: the spread of who conquers correlates with route-derived aggression across a seed sweep, and a warlike people and a peaceable one are both normal outcomes.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the Empires design pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A civilisation is what mixing makes, and it is not a creed
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: some civilisations form, whereby mixing cultures gives rise to philosophy and ethics, as removed from the initial religion-based creeds.

THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING. A CREED is what a people brought with them: a pantheon coined at a cradle, carried along a route, inherited by every daughter. A CIVILISATION is what happens when peoples MIX -- second-order, belonging to no single culture, about how one ought to live rather than which gods there are. Creeds are the migration's output and are already built; civilisations are the empire phase's output and CANNOT be generated at a cradle, because there is nothing yet to mix.

THE MIXING IS ALREADY THERE: region::culture is a culture_shares distribution and the assimilation machinery already moves it when ground changes hands. A region carrying two peoples in quantity, for a long time, is the condition to grow one from.

NOT SETTLED, AND NOT TO BE GUESSED AT BUILD TIME: whether a civilisation is a named record like a culture, a set of axes over the cultures composing it, or a lens on the existing shares; what it means for a polity to BELONG to one; whether it can outlive the polities that formed it.

DONE WHEN: civilisations arise only where mixing actually happened, are legible as distinct from the creeds beneath them, and a world with little mixing produces few or none.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-09, elicitation): A CIVILISATION IS A NAMED RECORD, like a culture, with member cultures and an ETHIC. Not a set of axes over the composing cultures, and not a lens on the existing shares.

A RECORD IS WHAT LETS IT OUTLIVE THE POLITIES THAT FORMED IT, which the other two candidates cannot supply: a lens dies the moment the shares beneath it move, so a civilisation would evaporate exactly when the design most wants it -- after the empire that raised it fragments. A record persists and the fragments inherit it. That property is load-bearing for the pass-2 handoff (see BL-823).

THE ETHIC IS THE FIELD THAT MAKES IT NOT-A-CREED: a creed answers which gods there are, an ethic answers how one ought to live. Second-order by construction, derived from what the member cultures disagreed about and settled, so it can only exist where mixing happened.

THE NAME IS COINED FROM THE TONGUES THAT MIXED, never from a bank of its own (world/tongue.hpp), and the standing rule holds without exception: sci-fi names, never an Earth list.

STILL OPEN: what an ethic is AS DATA, and what it means for a polity to BELONG to a civilisation as opposed to standing on ground that carries one.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, the Empires design pass); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Cultures are alike or opposed, and that is the engine of conquest
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09: cultures have similarities, and sometimes directly opposing views. This leads to conflict, and it becomes the engine for our simulated city states to begin an idea of conquest.

OPENED AS A DESIGN ASIDE (CIVILISATION.md sec Culture relations), NOT SETTLED. This item carries the work once the calls are answered.

SIMILARITY IS KINSHIP, and the substrate exists: the migration's family tree (BL-865). Two peoples are alike because they share an ancestor and parted recently -- earned by the migration rather than assigned.

OPPOSITION NEEDS A SECOND AXIS, because kinship alone gives DISTANT and not OPPOSED, and those differ: two peoples across a continent who never met are distant and have no quarrel. Three candidates, all from quantities that already exist -- the pantheon's own zeal/dominion; the farm class a people was coined on (BL-864), which is a material disagreement rather than a stated one; and contact itself, via culture_shares interpenetration.

THE FOUR OPEN CALLS, recorded in the doc and in the review queue: is opposition SYMMETRIC (grudges are directed; a disagreement about how to live may not be); does kinship DECAY or is the tree enough; does opposition CAUSE conquest or merely PERMIT it (feeding w_cult is the smaller change and keeps one scorer, a score of its own makes relations the engine Ben describes); and how does a civilisation relate to opposed cultures inside it.

DONE WHEN: the calls are answered, relations are derived from history rather than rolled, and a sweep shows both alliance-shaped and enmity-shaped worlds.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-09, elicitation) -- OPPOSITION IS SUPPLIED BY TWO AXES: the PANTHEON'S TEMPERAMENT (zeal, dominion) and the ORIGIN FARM CLASS (BL-864). Together, not either alone. CONTACT IS NOT AN AXIS.

WHY BOTH: the pantheon gives a STATED disagreement, the farm class a MATERIAL one. Temperament without material interest is a quarrel about nothing; material interest without temperament is a quarrel nobody will fight.

WHY NOT CONTACT: interpenetration says two peoples MET, which is a precondition for a quarrel rather than a cause of one -- and w_cult already reads the shares, so counting contact inside opposition would charge the same fact twice.

THE OTHER THREE CALLS, taken on Ben's behalf and open for overturning:
- SYMMETRIC (NR-815). Relations are a triangular matrix over cultures, not directed pairs. The directed layer already exists and does a different job: grudge records who wronged whom, at a place and a date.
- KINSHIP IS YEARS SINCE THE COMMON ANCESTOR, not hops (NR-816). Decay without a decay constant. REQUIRES BL-873 -- the coining year is a third discarded migration fact and the measure is worthless without it.
- FRACTURE GATES, INHERIT FOLLOWS (NR-817). No civilisation is coined across opposition above a bar; one that forms over residual opposition carries it as strain. Resolve was rejected as a forced outcome.

WHERE THE BAR SITS IS A MEASUREMENT, not a judgement: set it from a sweep producing both alliance-shaped and enmity-shaped worlds, never from a number picked to make one seed look right.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, elicitation); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Split the recorded span at 400 BCE, so Empires is its own 1600 years
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-09, elicitation, boundary and total revised by Ben the same day): THE EMPIRES PHASE RUNS FROM 400 BCE TO 1200 CE, AND PASS 1 COVERS 3,600 YEARS.

THE ARITHMETIC, which CIVILISATION.md sec The span is 400 BCE to 1200 CE owns and every other doc takes from:
  Culture -- the migration   2400 BCE -> 400 BCE    2,000 years
  Empires -- this phase       400 BCE -> 1200 CE    1,600 years
  Pass 1, total              2400 BCE -> 1200 CE    3,600 years

1200 CE IS UNMOVED, so the coast to 1560, pass 2 and the 1960 epoch are untouched (BL-831). What moved is where pass 1 STARTS and where it DIVIDES. The first cut of this item said 0 CE inside an unchanged 4,000-year pass; both numbers are superseded.

THIS IS THE PIECE NEXT_SESSION.md CALLED 'the natural next piece'. Rounds Culture and Empires currently replay THE SAME RECORDED AGE and both say so on screen; generation still emits one span. This item makes the split real.

400 BCE IS NOT A YEAR THE ENGINE ALREADY KNOWS, and the first cut of this item wrongly claimed the boundary was free because the sim's ancient arc ends at 0 CE. It does -- but the boundary is no longer there. Treat the split as real work: nothing in hard_coded_world.cpp or history_sim.cpp already stops at 400 BCE.

THE COAST IS CONFIRMED (Ben, 2026-09-09, resolving NR-818). COLONISATION.md ends the migration round when every habitable landmass carries some culture -- a derived year, not 400 BCE. Both rulings hold: the Culture round ends when the filling ends, and the world then COASTS to 400 BCE holding what migration left it, simulating nothing in between. Same device as 1200 -> 1560. WHAT MUST BE CHECKED ACROSS THE COAST is whatever accumulates on its own -- assimilation shares (BL-826) and grudge decay (BL-827) are the two named for the 1200 -> 1560 gap, and the same question applies here.

SIXTEEN HUNDRED YEARS IS THE CONSTRAINT ON THE PHASE. The arc -- communication, then conquest or union, then a stable dark age -- must fit in it. MEASURE BEFORE TUNING: the capacity ladder was calibrated over four thousand years, and whether its rungs still turn over believably in 1,600 out of a 3,600-year pass is an open question in CIVILISATION.md sec Open questions, not a licence to adjust constants.

COST NOTE: pass 1 is 400 years SHORTER than it was, which is a small relief against the region-count risk in NR-809 and not a solution to it.

RELATED READING: NR-810 (round 4 promises four thousand years and plays four hundred) is the surface symptom this boundary work should retire.

DONE WHEN: the two rounds play DIFFERENT spans, neither screen still says it is replaying the same age, a world coasts cleanly from its fill year to 400 BCE with nothing reset and nothing accumulating lost, and world_determinism is unchanged.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-09, elicitation notes); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A population centre is what the network can feed and rule, not a demographic accident
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-09 (elicitation notes): the sparse road network 'gives us actual population centres, DERIVED BY POSSIBLE SUPPLY AND GOVERNANCE'.

THAT GIVES region::centres A CAUSE IT CURRENTLY LACKS. Today a centre is promoted when urban_population crosses region_centre_heads (10,000) -- a threshold on demography alone, blind to whether anything can reach or rule the place. Under this item a centre stands where supply can reach it AND where a seat can govern it, so the urban map is downstream of the road map.

IT IS WHAT MAKES THE SPARSE PATTERN HOLD RATHER THAN DRIFT. Centres do not appear because population crossed a threshold in isolation; they appear where a network put them, which is why the map stays legible as population grows. Without this, BL-866's sparse seats sit on a dense centre field and the two disagree.

DEPENDS ON BOTH HALVES: BL-866 supplies the seat that does the governing, BL-837 supplies the reach that does the supplying. It cannot be built before either.

NOT SETTLED, AND NOT TO BE GUESSED: whether governance reach and supply reach are ONE quantity or two; and whether a centre that loses its supply is razed, frozen, or demoted. Razing is the destructive reading and centres_razed already exists for the sack case -- reuse it only if the meaning really is the same.

DONE WHEN: centre placement correlates with reach rather than with population alone, a region cut off from its seat stops growing centres, and a world with a poor network has visibly fewer centres than one with a good one at the same total population.

items.author: Claude (2026-09-09, taken on Ben's behalf under NR-816)
items.title: Retain the year a culture was coined, so kinship can be measured in years
items.design:
THE THIRD DISCARDED MIGRATION FACT, and the smallest of the three.

BL-865 retained culture::parent and culture::origin_farm_class after CIVILISATION.md found the descent tree was being built and thrown away. The same is true of WHEN each culture was coined: the migration knows the year at every founding, and nothing keeps it.

WHY IT IS NEEDED NOW: NR-816 settles kinship as YEARS SINCE THE COMMON ANCESTOR rather than tree hops, and that measure is worthless without the years. The tree runs 9-10 deep over 676 and 929 cultures, so hop count is coarse AND blind to timing -- two peoples four hops apart may have parted three thousand years ago or three hundred, and those are not the same relationship. Time is decay without a decay constant, which is the dial this layer keeps refusing.

THE SHAPE IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED. One integer on culture, written where the daughter is coined, in exactly the form BL-865 used. Ids are handed out in arrival order and a parent is always at a lower index than its daughter, so a walk toward the root strictly decreases -- the common-ancestor walk is bounded and cannot loop.

BLOCKS BL-870 (culture relations). File it first because it is cheap and because the measure cannot be written without it.

DONE WHEN: every culture carries its coining year, a cradle culture's year is the span's start rather than a sentinel that reads as a real date, and the years-to-common-ancestor walk is exercised by the colonisation harness.
